messages.subject: Multinomial Logistic Help
parts:
Hi all,

I have data which are multinomial. Specifically, each sample is a fixed count to roughly 200 organisms each of which is classified to genus. I've run several other count based models that ignore this fact, and now would like to see if there's any difference in the inferences I'm making if I actually remain faithful to the idea that there is a fixed count. In any case, I also have a hierarchy on the parameters for each genus, the hyperparameters of which I have set to have noninformative priors (I have this same hierarchy for my other models too, and they have run just fine). Anyway, I tried the model below and I got the following error:

TRANSLATING MODEL 'mult2_mod' FROM Stan CODE TO C++ CODE NOW.
Error in stanc(file = file, model_code = model_code, model_name = model_name,  :
  failed to parse Stan model 'mult2_mod' with error message:
EXPECTATION FAILURE LOCATION: file=input; line=45, column=5

    taxon_ct[i] ~ multinomial(softmax(phi[i]),n[i]);
    ^-- here


DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:
no matches for function name="multinomial_log"
    arg 0 type=int[1]
    arg 1 type=vector
    arg 2 type=int
available function signatures for multinomial_log:
0.  multinomial_log(int[1], vector) : real
unknown distribution=multinomial
Parser expecting: "}"

I think I have the correct forms in my call to the multinomial distribution, i.e. a vector of parameters, softmax(phi[i]), which is a simplex of length j (defined in transformed parameters) and an integer, n[i], representing the fixed count. So, I'm unsure why I'm getting the error. Can someone help? Here is my model:

mult2_mod <- '
data {
  int<lower=0> I; //number of sites
  int<lower=0> J; //number of taxa
  int<lower=0> n[I]; //number of taxa identified
  vector[I] logcond; //log(conductivity) value at each site
  int<lower=0> taxon_ct[I,J]; //count of taxon at each site
  real l_alpha_1; //set first taxon log alpha = 0
  real beta_1; //set first taxon beta = 0
  real prec_1; //set inverse variance to = 0.00000001
}
parameters {
  real mu_logalpha;
  real<lower=0> tau_logalpha;
  real mu_beta;
  real<lower=0> tau_beta;
  real<lower=0> rho;
  vector[J-1] beta_2;
  vector[J-1] log_alpha_2;
  vector<lower=0>[J-1] prec_2;
}
transformed parameters {
  vector[J] phi[I];
  vector[J] log_alpha;
  vector[J] beta;
  vector<lower=0>[J] prec;
  vector<lower=0>[J] gam;
  log_alpha[1] <- l_alpha_1;
  beta[1] <- beta_1;
  prec[1] <- prec_1;
  for (j in 2:J) {
    log_alpha[j] <- log_alpha_2[j-1];
    beta[j] <- beta_2[j-1];
    prec[j] <- prec_2[j-1];
  }
  for (j in 1:J){
    gam[j] <- pow(prec[j],-0.5);
    for(i in 1:I){
      phi[i,j] <- log_alpha[j] - square((beta[j] - logcond[i])/gam[j]);
    }
  }
}
model {
for(i in 1:I){
    taxon_ct[i] ~ multinomial(softmax(phi[i]),n[i]);
  }
mu_logalpha ~ normal(0,sqrt(1000));
tau_logalpha ~ uniform(0,100);
mu_beta ~ normal(0,sqrt(1000));
tau_beta ~ uniform(0,100);
rho ~ gamma(1,1);
log_alpha_2 ~ normal(mu_logalpha,tau_logalpha);
beta_2 ~ normal(mu_beta,tau_beta);
prec_2 ~ gamma(1, rho);
}
generated quantities {
  vector<lower=0>[J] alpha;
  vector[J] XC90;
  vector[J] XC75;
  vector[J] XC95;
  alpha <- exp(log_alpha);
  XC95 <- 1.644854*gam + beta;
  XC90 <- 1.281552*gam + beta;
  XC75 <- 0.6744898*gam + beta;
}
'
